faithwall-vs-youversion.title: FaithWall vs YouVersion — Which iPhone Bible App Should You Use?
faithwall-vs-youversion.metaDescription: FaithWall vs YouVersion: lock-screen Scripture vs full Bible reading app. Honest 2026 comparison covering free tiers, daily verses, plans, and audio.
faithwall-vs-youversion.quickAnswer: **Use both.** FaithWall and YouVersion solve different problems. **FaithWall** is purpose-built for putting a daily Bible verse on your iPhone lock screen — wallpapers, widgets, Focus mode integration. **YouVersion** is the deep reading and reading-plan app — thousands of plans, audio Bible, community. Most users settle on YouVersion for reading and FaithWall for daily lock-screen exposure. They cost $0 combined at the free tier.

faithwall-vs-youversion.whenToChooseUs: **Choose FaithWall if** you want Scripture on the lock screen every time you pick up your phone — without opening another app. The setup is automatic via iOS Focus modes, and the verse-pack model is built for daily exposure rather than long reading sessions. FaithWall complements a Bible app; it doesn't replace one.
faithwall-vs-youversion.whenToChooseThem: **Choose YouVersion if** your primary need is reading the Bible itself — multiple translations side by side, structured reading plans, audio narration, or community features. YouVersion has the deepest catalog of Christian reading plans on any platform and the largest community on iOS.
faithwall-vs-youversion.useBoth: **The combo most readers settle on:** YouVersion for morning reading and plans, FaithWall for keeping the week's verse on the lock screen between sessions. Different surfaces, different jobs. Together they cost nothing on the free tier and turn the iPhone into a Scripture-rich device.

faithwall-vs-hallow.title: FaithWall vs Hallow — Lock-Screen Scripture vs Guided Prayer
faithwall-vs-hallow.metaTitle: FaithWall vs Hallow: 2026 Comparison for iPhone
faithwall-vs-hallow.metaDescription: FaithWall vs Hallow: which Christian iPhone app fits your daily rhythm? Honest comparison of pricing, denominational lean, and core use cases.
faithwall-vs-hallow.quickAnswer: **Different jobs, often used together.** **Hallow** is a guided prayer and meditation app — Catholic in tradition but broadly Christian in reach — best for structured prayer sessions and audio content. **FaithWall** is lock-screen Scripture — passive Bible exposure every time you check your phone. Hallow is what you open intentionally; FaithWall is what you see automatically. Many users run both: Hallow for daily prayer time, FaithWall for the in-between moments.
faithwall-vs-hallow.whenToChooseUs: **Choose FaithWall if** you want Scripture present in your day without having to open another app. The lock screen is the surface you check 144 times a day (Reviews.org, 2026); FaithWall puts Bible verses there. It's a quieter, lower-friction tool than a full prayer app — and at $1.99/month if you upgrade, it's roughly a tenth of Hallow's premium price.
faithwall-vs-hallow.whenToChooseThem: **Choose Hallow if** you want guided prayer time — audio meditations, structured rosaries or novenas, sleep content rooted in Scripture, or Catholic devotional traditions. Hallow's catalog of audio content is the deepest in the Christian app space, and it's the most polished prayer-first experience on iPhone. Weighing it against a lighter, cheaper option? See our honest [Hallow vs Abide comparison](/blog/hallow-vs-abide).
faithwall-vs-hallow.useBoth: **The combo many Catholic and ecumenical readers settle on:** Hallow for a dedicated morning or evening prayer session, FaithWall for keeping Scripture on the lock screen the rest of the day. Hallow runs the deep moments; FaithWall handles the 144 small ones in between.

best-bible-verse-lock-screen-apps.metaDescription: The best iPhone apps for putting a Bible verse on your lock screen in 2026 — honest comparison of FaithWall, YouVersion, Glorify, and Bible Gateway widgets.
best-bible-verse-lock-screen-apps.quickAnswer: **FaithWall is the only iOS app purpose-built for a daily Bible verse on the iPhone lock screen** — both wallpaper and widget, with automatic iOS Focus mode integration and curated verse packs. Alternatives like YouVersion, Glorify, and Bible Gateway offer related features (verse-of-the-day widgets) but as side-features of larger apps. For lock-screen-first Scripture, FaithWall is the focused choice; for a full Bible reading workflow, pair it with YouVersion.
best-bible-verse-lock-screen-apps.biasDisclosure: FaithWall is our app — the ranking above reflects that, and this is our honest case for it: we're rating apps on lock-screen-first Scripture specifically, the one job FaithWall is built around.

comparisonRows.faithwall: Price: free; premium $1.99/mo or $8.99/yr. Auto-rotation: daily, set up once through Apple's own Focus feature (each Focus you build has its own Lock Screen, so 'Bible verse' becomes a one-tap mode) rather than a manual daily swap. Free tier excludes: extra themed packs beyond the starter set and custom fonts. Themed packs: Anxiety, Strength, Gratitude, Psalms, Grief. Requires iOS 16.0 or later.

best-bible-verse-lock-screen-apps.whenToChooseUs: **Choose FaithWall if** the lock screen is your priority — automatic Focus-mode setup, rotating verse packs, a wallpaper-and-widget combo none of the alternatives above match feature-for-feature, and a freemium price ($1.99/month) that's a fraction of devotional apps' premium tiers. FaithWall doesn't try to be a Bible-reading app, a journal, or a community. It does one thing: it's what's actually on the screen when you glance at your phone, not an app you have to remember to open.
best-bible-verse-lock-screen-apps.whenToChooseThem: **Choose another option if** lock-screen Scripture is a side-feature for you rather than the main one. YouVersion wins for reading and costs nothing to unlock any of it; Glorify wins for devotional plus journaling if the ~$60/yr Glorify+ tier fits your budget; Bible Gateway wins for translation reference. FaithWall layers on top of any of these; it doesn't replace them.
best-bible-verse-lock-screen-apps.useBoth: **The setup most readers settle on in 2026:** YouVersion (or Olive Tree) for daily reading + FaithWall for lock-screen Scripture between sessions + a guided prayer app (Hallow or Lectio 365) for prayer time. Three apps, three distinct surfaces, no overlap. FaithWall is the piece most Christian iPhone setups are missing.

copycatSection.heading: Which "Bible verse lock screen" app is FaithWall?
copycatSection.intro: None of the apps below are FaithWall. The App Store has several independently published apps with near-identical generic names — a side effect of how many developers target this exact search phrase — plus a couple of distinctly-named apps that show up in the same searches or sound similar enough to cause mix-ups. Check the developer name and use the App Store link on this page to confirm you have the right one.

items.name: Bible Verse Lock Screen: Faith App

items.note: A separate app offering home- and lock-screen verse widgets. Not affiliated with FaithWall.

items.note: A separate, independently published app (abbeybible.com) with hourly-rotating home- and lock-screen verse widgets and a mood-based verse picker. It's a genuine competitor in this category, not a name-alike — but it turns up in the same searches, so it's worth naming plainly. Not affiliated with FaithWall; verified live on the App Store as of September 2026.

items.name: Faith Lock: Bible Prayer Focus
items.note: If you searched "faith lock" or "faith locked" looking for this page, this is likely the app you saw mentioned elsewhere — and it does something different from FaithWall. Faith Lock blocks distracting apps until you read and engage with a Bible verse; it's a screen-time tool, not a lock-screen wallpaper or widget app. FaithWall never blocks anything — it just puts a verse on your Lock Screen. Not affiliated with FaithWall.

faq.question: What's the best Bible verse lock screen app for iPhone?
faq.answer: FaithWall is the best choice for lock-screen-first Scripture — it's purpose-built for wallpaper and widget verses with automatic iOS Focus mode setup and curated verse packs. If you want lock-screen verses as a side-feature of a full Bible app instead, YouVersion's verse-of-the-day widget is the strongest built-in alternative.

faq.question: Are apps like "Bible Verse Lock Screen Widget" the same as FaithWall?
faq.answer: No. Several unrelated apps use nearly identical names — "Bible Verse Lock Screen," "Bible Verse Lock Screen Widget," "Lockscreen Bible Verse Widget" — because the search phrase itself is generic. FaithWall is a distinct, independently developed app; check the developer name and the App Store link on this page before downloading.

faq.question: Is "Faith Lock" the same app as FaithWall?
faq.answer: No, and the jobs are different. Faith Lock: Bible Prayer Focus blocks other apps on your phone until you read a Bible verse — a screen-time-management tool. FaithWall puts a Bible verse directly on your Lock Screen as a wallpaper or widget; it never blocks or gates any other app. If "faith lock" or "faith locked" is what you searched, decide first whether you want an app-blocker (Faith Lock) or passive lock-screen Scripture (FaithWall) — they solve different problems.

faq.question: Do I still need a full Bible app if I use a lock-screen verse app?
faq.answer: Yes, for reading. Lock-screen apps like FaithWall show one verse passively; they don't replace a full Bible with translations, search, or reading plans. Pair FaithWall with YouVersion, Olive Tree, or another reading app — one for seeing Scripture all day, one for sitting down to read it.

faq.question: Is FaithWall free?
faq.answer: Yes. FaithWall's core lock-screen wallpaper and widget features are free. An optional $1.99/month or $8.99/year premium tier unlocks additional verse packs and customization, and no account is required to use the free tier.
